findings.description: Accepted suppression lines (race:^juce::<Class>::<function>( and deadlock:^juce::...() apply to every frame of both access stacks (and to the allocation stack or global name of the location), not only the top frame. In T-304, JUCE frames lie above wrapper code on the parameter path (setValueNotifyingHost -> sendValueChangedMessageToListeners -> wrapper listener) and the state path (S-310 action 2 updates JUCE parameters inside setStateInformation), so an accepted line naming such a function hides every wrapper race beneath it. T-092's own passing example deadlock:^juce::CriticalSection::enter( suppresses every lock-order report involving any juce::CriticalSection, wrapper-owned ones included. Both canaries test the anchor syntax, not the scope of a suppression.
findings.lens: technical correctness; CI platform coverage; past lessons
findings.conditions: T-304 under TSan shows a JUCE-internal report on the parameter or state path (anticipated by ENVIRONMENT section 5), so the suppression names a JUCE function that also lies on a wrapper race's call path
findings.root_cause: the checker constrains where a frame name starts, while ThreadSanitizer's race:/deadlock: types match any frame; only race_top: is limited to the top frame
findings.traces_to: tests/ci/check_tsan_supp.py, tests/py/test_tsan_supp_check.py (T-092), tests/ci/tsan_canary_named.cpp, ci.yml host-tsan, ENVIRONMENT section 5, tests/juce/host_test.cpp T-304, S-310 action 2, D-094, R-051, R-078, L-20261029T000000Z
findings.failure_path: S-320 host-tsan reports a race with top frames in JUCE and the test thread passing through juce::AudioProcessorParameter::setValueNotifyingHost(float) -> tsan.supp gains race:^juce::AudioProcessorParameter::setValueNotifyingHost( (T-092 accepts it; DEVIATIONS entry) -> green -> FolkProcessor::parameterValueChanged(int, float) races with processBlock beneath that frame and is suppressed for good -> clicks or crashes on automation in hosts
findings.mitigation: TEST_CHALLENGE amendment: the checker accepts only race_top:^juce::<Name>(::<Name>)+( and refuses race: lines; no deadlock: line without an owner's answer at G-004; a third frozen canary tsan_canary_scope.cpp where juce::CanaryBox::call(void(*)(int), int) calls a racing canary_ns::touch(int): under the accepted line race_top:^juce::CanaryBox::call( it must still exit 66 (a race: line would make it exit 0)
findings.mitigation_adds: a negative control on suppression scope, the property R-051 was about; suppressions can no longer reach wrapper frames below a JUCE caller

findings.description: ENVIRONMENT section 5 allows a suppression only for 'a report whose every frame lies in JUCE module code' and calls 'a report with a frame in plugins/ or core/' a defect. No T-304 report can qualify: every stack holds frames from tests/juce/host_test.cpp and libstdc++ (std::thread::_State_impl::_M_run), and every audio-thread stack holds FolkProcessor::processBlock from plugins/.
findings.conditions: any JUCE-internal TSan report in T-304
findings.root_cause: the criterion is stated over whole stacks instead of the racing accesses' top frames
findings.traces_to: plan/ENVIRONMENT.md section 5 (host-tsan row), ci.yml host-tsan, T-304, F-1
findings.failure_path: S-320 host-tsan red on a JUCE-internal report -> the strict reading forbids any suppression (blocked, or an unfixable 'defect'); a loose reading has no bound on which frames may lie outside JUCE, which feeds F-1
findings.mitigation: state the rule on top frames: both accesses' #0 frames lie in JUCE module code, and no frame above the first test-harness frame lies in plugins/ or core/ (consistent with race_top: of F-1)

findings.description: The sanitiser-exclusion grep (no_sanitize|fno-sanitize|__tsan_ignore|tsan_ignore over CMakeLists.txt, plugins, core, tests/juce) misses: removal of the flag (string(REPLACE "-fsanitize=thread" ...), list(REMOVE_ITEM ...)); a subdirectory or cmake/ module that builds the JUCE modules into a separate library with reset flags; files outside the four paths (cmake/, CMakePresets.json, third_party/); and TSan dynamic annotations that hide races without removing instrumentation (AnnotateIgnoreReadsBegin/WritesBegin, AnnotateBenignRaceSized, AnnotateHappensBefore/After, __tsan_acquire/__tsan_release). Without -q, grep exits 2 when a path is missing or unreadable even with a match, and the if treats that as no match. R-077's nm check still proves only that one translation unit is instrumented.
findings.conditions: a JUCE report that no accepted line can express (anonymous namespace, template-only frames, a thread-leak or mutex report) and an implementer who works around it against the prose rule
findings.root_cause: a negative string search stands in for a positive check that each object is instrumented
findings.traces_to: ci.yml host-tsan 'No source or build file switches the sanitiser off' and 'Concurrency test' (nm), ENVIRONMENT section 5, R-077, R-078
findings.failure_path: JUCE report not expressible -> JUCE modules built as a static library in cmake/juce.cmake with -fsanitize=thread removed from CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS -> grep finds nothing -> nm finds __tsan_init in the wrapper -> green -> wrapper-against-JUCE races invisible (round 4 incident 1)
findings.mitigation: (optional, remote) for every object file in build-tsan compiled from JUCE module or plugins/ sources, nm -u lists __tsan_func_entry; widen the grep to fsanitize|Annotate(Ignore|BenignRace|HappensBefore|HappensAfter)|__tsan_ over all tracked files except the workflow; test grep's status explicitly (rc=0; grep ... || rc=$?; test $rc -eq 1)
findings.mitigation_adds: a positive, per-object proof of instrumentation that does not depend on how an exclusion is spelled

findings.description: In a confirmation round, confirm is 'valid only if the pass condition holds where pairs exist' (D-053, GATES), so for a gate without pairs nothing checks the 'wrong:' line; S-LISTEN's Done when checks scores only and accepts '(or each has confirm)'. G-L1 and G-L4 (and G-L5 unless S-REF finds 12 notes) have no pairs (C-051), and they are the reed gates a later reed change is expected to reopen.
findings.conditions: a confirmation round of a gate without pairs in which the owner names a demo as wrong while answering confirm
findings.root_cause: R-079's fix restored only the score clause of the frozen pass condition for confirmations
findings.traces_to: D-053 confirmation rule, GATES G-L allowed responses, S-LISTEN Done when, HANDOFF section 9, R-068, R-079
findings.failure_path: G-L1 harmonica proceed (wrong: none) -> G-L3 iterate changes core/src/reed.cpp -> G-L1 confirmation -> owner: 'wrong: -08-bend', confirm -> valid by the wording -> Done when passes -> the pull request presents the harmonica as confirmed with a bend the owner called wrong
findings.mitigation: confirm (like proceed) is valid only if the full pass condition holds: the score where pairs exist and, always, 'wrong: none'; otherwise ask once as for proceed; S-LISTEN Done when requires 'wrong: none' in each gate's latest valid attempt or a rescope naming the demo
findings.mitigation_adds: the frozen demo clause applies to the audio that ships, for the three gates without pairs

findings.description: A confirmation round can close only with confirm. (a) For a gate with pairs previously closed with proceed-with-rescope over a score above 8, the confirmation usually scores above 8 again, so confirm is invalid. D-053 says to ask 'as for proceed' (iterate, proceed-with-rescope, stop), but GATES' confirmation responses exclude proceed-with-rescope, and S-LISTEN's Done when lets a gate needing confirmation pass only with confirm. proceed-without-pairs after two voids and stop hit the same wall. (b) The trigger compares against 'the commit its evidence was built from', and nothing makes a confirmation replace that commit, so every later check (before S-REVIEW-DELTA, before the pull request, after each S-INTEGRATE fix) re-triggers on identical audio and reaches the two-confirmation cap.
findings.conditions: a gate with pairs (G-L3 or G-L2) closed with proceed-with-rescope because it scored above 8, followed by a shared change in its family (R-068's premise); (b) alone needs only one confirmation followed by any later check
findings.root_cause: R-079's fix defined confirm's validity but not the other closures or the confirmation's commit
findings.traces_to: D-053, GATES G-L allowed responses and branches, S-LISTEN Done when, S-INTEGRATE action 3, R-079, R-080
findings.failure_path: G-L2 rescope at 10/12 -> G-L5 iterate changes pluck.cpp -> G-L2 confirmation 10/12 -> confirm invalid -> the owner repeats the rescope (not an allowed confirmation response) -> the implementer halts, forces an unwanted iterate (counted towards the round limit), or records the rescope as confirm; separately, a confirmed gate re-triggers at S-INTEGRATE action 3 on unchanged audio
findings.mitigation: confirmation rounds also accept proceed-with-rescope: <text>; for a gate previously closed by rescope, confirm is valid when the score is no higher than the score the rescope accepted; each confirmation records its evidence commit, which becomes the gate's commit for later checks; S-LISTEN Done when: each gate's latest closing response is valid and its recorded commit renders the same demos as the head commit
findings.mitigation_adds: every gate has a defined closure and identical audio is never re-heard

findings.description: confirm-again (allowed when a third confirmation would start) reads naturally as 'I confirm again', meaning close without listening, whereas it is meant to start a third confirmation round; the only alternative offered is stop (DR-15: the instrument is dropped).
findings.conditions: a third confirmation of one gate (an iterate ping-pong in one family, R-080)
findings.root_cause: response name chosen for the cap without defined semantics or a non-destructive exit
findings.traces_to: D-053, GATES G-L allowed responses, R-080
findings.failure_path: third confirmation due -> owner answers confirm-again -> the implementer closes the gate on it -> audio never heard ships as confirmed (R-068's harm); or the owner who meant closure is made to listen a fourth time
findings.mitigation: rename it start-confirmation, state that it starts a listening round, and add proceed-with-rescope: <text> (accept the unheard change, recorded) beside stop
findings.mitigation_adds: unambiguous cap response and a non-destructive exit

findings.description: D-053 reopens a gate only if the demos differ AND git diff -- core/ presets/ tools/folk-render/ is non-empty; a render-changing edit outside those paths (top-level CMakeLists.txt compile options such as -ffast-math, -O3 or FTZ, or a cmake/ module) changes the demos but reopens nothing.
findings.conditions: a fix after a gate closes changes compile options outside the listed paths
findings.root_cause: the output trigger was added as a conjunct to the path trigger instead of replacing it
findings.traces_to: D-053 confirmation rule, S-REVIEW-DELTA, S-INTEGRATE action 3, R-068, R-080
findings.failure_path: S-REVIEW-DELTA denormal or performance fix adds a top-level compile option -> demos differ -> no listed path changed -> no confirmation -> the pull request presents audio the owner never heard
findings.mitigation: let the demo comparison alone decide (optional; Medium)

findings.description: D-051 permits a private reference only while the redistributable pool has fewer than 12 notes, but S-REF searches to 14, with (d) Philharmonia last; and build_evidence.py routes pairs to the public pairs/ 'when every one of the 12 references is redistributable' and skips pairs only if one of 'the 12' is absent, ignoring the 13th and 14th (control) references.
findings.conditions: sources (a) to (c) yield 12 or 13 usable redistributable mandolin notes (C-051 found none)
findings.root_cause: R-081's change (14 notes) was not carried into D-051 or into the routing and absence rules of S-340
findings.traces_to: D-051, S-REF action 3, S-340 action 1(b) and 2, gate-evidence.yml (--only-redistributable), D-053, R-081
findings.failure_path: S-REF indexes 12 Wikimedia mandolin notes then two Philharmonia notes without a D-### justification (Rule 15) -> CI gate-evidence fetches redistributable rows only -> control references absent -> build_evidence fails or falls back to repeating controls (R-071); publication is blocked by the redistributable-only fetch, so not Critical
findings.mitigation: S-REF indexes a private note only while the redistributable pool is below 12; routing, absence handling and MANIFEST derived_from consider all 14 references
findings.mitigation_adds: consistency with Rule 15 and fail-closed routing for controls

findings.description: D-053 says confirmation seeds 1000g + 900 + 10j + k 'never collide', but j is unbounded once confirm-again is given: j = 20 gives 1000(g+1) + 100 + k, the seed of attempt k of round 1 of gate g+1.
findings.root_cause: seed range for j not bounded
findings.traces_to: D-053 seeds; enumeration in this round
findings.failure_path: 20th confirmation of G-L1 reuses G-L2 round 1's key, which is decoded and committed
findings.mitigation: bound j below 10 or move confirmations to a separate range

summary: Round 5 (last). 10 numbered findings plus 20 restatements. New or residual: High 4 (F-1 residual R-051/R-078 suppression scope, plausible; F-3 residual R-078 exclusion grep, remote; F-4 residual R-079 confirm ignores wrong-demo line on gates without pairs, plausible; F-5 new, confirmation cannot close a rescoped gate and does not re-baseline, plausible), Medium 4 (F-2, F-6, F-7, F-8), Low 2 (F-9; F-10 speculative). No Critical. The round-4 anchor form works for function frames and the named canary proves it, but neither canary tests scope; the confirmation rule fixed the score clause but not the demo clause, other closures, or the commit it compares against.
